punchline: Students paid to solve a puzzle they already liked played with it less once the pay stopped.
thirty_sec: In Edward Deci's puzzle study, students who already liked a puzzle were paid on the second day only. In the break they played with it more while paid, and on the third day, with the pay gone, significantly less than a group that was never paid. Daniel Pink uses the result to argue that rewards can turn play into work. Later critics say the drop may simply be a reaction to losing the reward.
